result.markdown: --- title: "Foundations: SIR theory and the Julia workflow" course-unit: ch01-foundations status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - The conceptual anchor of the course: derive the SIR model of Kermack & McKendrick (1927) from first principles. - Read off the two quantities that govern every epidemic: the reproduction number $R_0$ and the epidemic threshold. - Solve it with the modern **SciML** stack and verify conservation, the threshold, and the analytic **final-size** relation. ## Assumptions & equations {.smaller} Closed, well-mixed population; mass-action transmission; constant recovery; permanent immunity. Force of infection $\lambda=\beta c I/N$: $$ \frac{\mathrm{d}S}{\mathrm{d}t}=-\lambda S,\quad \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}=\lambda S-\gamma I,\quad \frac{\mathrm{d}R}{\mathrm{d}t}=\gamma I. $$ {#eq-s-ch01-sir} $$ R_0=\frac{\beta c}{\gamma},\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}>0 \iff \frac{S}{N}>\frac{1}{R_0}, $$ {#eq-s-ch01-r0} $$ s_\infty = s_0\exp\!\bigl(-R_0(1-s_\infty)\bigr),\quad s_0=S(0)/N. $$ {#eq-s-ch01-finalsize} ## Julia API: solve & analyse ::: {#cell-s-ch01-solve .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using OrdinaryDiffEq, NonlinearSolve function sir_ode!(du, u, p, t) S, I, R = u # state positional, parameters by field λ = p.β * p.c * I / p.N du[1] = -λ * S; du[2] = λ * S - p.γ * I; du[3] = p.γ * I; return nothing end u0 = [990.0, 10.0, 0.0]; tspan = (0.0, 80.0) p = (β = 0.05, c = 10.0, γ = 0.25, N = 1000.0) sol = solve(ODEProblem(sir_ode!, u0, tspan, p), Tsit5(); saveat = 0.5) R₀ = p.β * p.c / p.γ; s₀ = u0[1] / p.N s_inf = solve(NonlinearProblem((s, R0) -> s - s₀ * exp(-R0 * (1 - s)), 0.2, R₀), NewtonRaphson()).u (R₀, round(s_inf; digits = 3), round(1 - s_inf; digits = 3)) # R0, s∞, attack rate ``` ::: {#s-ch01-solve .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (2.0, 0.2, 0.8) ``` ::: ::: ## Generated result ::: {#cell-fig-s-ch01-sir .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using CairoMakie t = sol.t; S = sol[1, :]; I = sol[2, :]; R = sol[3, :] fig = Figure(size = (760, 400)) ax = Axis(fig[1,1]; xlabel = "day", ylabel = "individuals", title = "SIR baseline, R₀ = 2") lines!(ax, t, S; color = :steelblue, linewidth = 3, label = "S") lines!(ax, t, I; color = :firebrick, linewidth = 3, label = "I") lines!(ax, t, R; color = :seagreen, linewidth = 3, label = "R") hlines!(ax, [p.N / R₀]; color = :black, linestyle = :dash, label = "S = N/R₀") axislegend(ax; position = :rc); fig ``` ::: {#fig-s-ch01-sir .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Baseline SIR ($R_0=2$). The dashed line marks $S/N=1/R_0$; the infectious curve peaks exactly where $S$ crosses it. ::: ::: ## Validation Population conserved; infectious peak sits on the threshold; long-run $S/N$ matches the analytic $s_\infty$: ::: {#cell-s-ch01-check .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} cons = all(u -> isapprox(sum(u), p.N; atol = 1e-6), sol.u) peak = isapprox(S[argmax(I)] / p.N, 1 / R₀; atol = 0.01) sol_long = solve(ODEProblem(sir_ode!, u0, (0.0, 400.0), p), Tsit5(); reltol = 1e-10, abstol = 1e-10, save_everystep = false) fsize = isapprox(sol_long.u[end][1] / p.N, s_inf; atol = 1e-3) (cons, peak, fsize) ``` ::: {#s-ch01-check .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (true, true, true) ``` ::: ::: All `true`: conservation, threshold, and final size are confirmed. ## Limitations & roadmap - The deterministic ODE is the population **mean** — no extinction, super-spreading, or small-outbreak noise. - Homogeneous mixing ignores age, space, contact structure; exponential infectious periods are a convenience. - The book relaxes each assumption in turn: discrete-time & stochastic → jump processes → SDEs → agent-based → observation, inference, control. ::: {.notes} Derive the mass-action term from contacts × prevalence × transmission probability, and show that summing the equations gives conservation. Explain R₀ as expected secondary infections in a fully susceptible population, and that the peak occurs exactly at S/N = 1/R₀. The final-size relation is transcendental, which is why NonlinearSolve is used. Use this chapter to preview the whole book. ::: ## Learn more - Book chapter: [Foundations](../../chapters/01-foundations.html) - Pluto notebook: [`01-foundations.jl`](../../notebooks/chapters/01-foundations.jl) - [OrdinaryDiffEq](https://docs.sciml.ai/OrdinaryDiffEq/stable/) · [NonlinearSolve](https://docs.sciml.ai/NonlinearSolve/stable/)
